blockingIssues.description: `python/runners/run_workflow.py` is the actual workflow subprocess entry point spawned by the server, but it still lacks direct `init_sentry()` / `flush_sentry()` coverage, so startup/import-time failures can occur before Sentry is active.
Route and module error boundaries render `RouteErrorView` without calling `Sentry.captureException`, so route-boundary errors are not reported to Sentry.
`python/core/logging.py` still uses hardcoded named loggers (`urllib3`, `playwright`), so the implementation does not satisfy the explicit `getLogger(__name__)` requirement.
`python/actions/engagement/follow/filter.py` still contains Cyrillic in non-selector text-matching logic, exceeding the documented selector-only exception.

`server/shared/asyncHandler.ts` only accepts handlers returning `Promise<void>`, but current async routes commonly return `Promise<Response>`, so the utility is not ready for clean downstream adoption.
The persisted verification log claims `python -m pytest python/tests -q` exited 0 while also recording `221 passed, 1 failed`, so VAL-FOUND-010 is not credibly satisfied.

appliedUpdates.description: Updated `install_frontend` and `install_server` to use `cd <dir> && npm install`, matching the mission npm-install gotcha guidance and avoiding the spurious `anti: file:..` dependency.
Documented `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` plus the required `env.ts -> shared/sentry.ts` bootstrap ordering in `.factory/library/environment.md`.
Documented that the server launches workflow subprocesses through `python/runners/run_workflow.py`, which then delegates to `python.runners.workflow.entrypoint.main()`.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add scoped-validation and non-refactor modes (for translation-only and verification-only features), and align `followedProcedure` expectations with those lighter-weight paths.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Multiple foundation reviews (server-pino-logging, dead-code-removal, sentry-frontend, russian-translation, foundation-verify) independently flagged that workers followed targeted procedures and scoped validation while still reporting `followedProcedure: true` against a refactor-centric skill.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify whether named third-party logger suppression inside `python/core/logging.py` is an allowed exception to the `getLogger(__name__)` rule; otherwise tighten the implementation requirement to remove that ambiguity.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The current contract says every `getLogger()` call must use `__name__`, but `python/core/logging.py` configures `urllib3` and `playwright` by explicit logger name, which reviewers could not reconcile as either allowed or forbidden without additional guidance.
